_meta.description: Fixed liturgical texts for the Divine Liturgy (Chrysostom and Basil) — invariable content

opening-doxology.exclamation: Blessed is the Kingdom of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

glory-now-doxology: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

pre-trisagion-litany._note: Slavonic-tradition short litany between the Kontakia and the Trisagion. Default-on; jurisdictions that omit it (e.g. Greek practice) set manifest.rubrics.omitPreTrisagionLitany = true on their overlay.
pre-trisagion-litany.deaconPray: Let us pray to the Lord.
pre-trisagion-litany.priestAges: And unto ages of ages. Amen.

hierarch-commemoration._note: Petition text for the hierarchs, referenced from the Great and Augmented litanies via '@@hierarch-commemoration.<litany>' sentinels. Parish overlays should override THESE keys (not the petition arrays themselves) to name their primate/diocesan/auxiliary bishops without copying the full petition list. The sentinel resolver lives in assembler.js (resolveFixedRef).
hierarch-commemoration.greatLitany: For our Archbishop N., for the honorable presbytery, the diaconate in Christ, all the clergy and the people, let us pray to the Lord.
hierarch-commemoration.augmentedLitany: Again we pray for our Archbishop N., and for our Bishop [or Archbishop] N.

great-litany.opening: In peace, let us pray to the Lord.
petitions: For the peace from above, and for the salvation of our souls, let us pray to the Lord.
For the peace of the whole world, the welfare of the holy churches of God, and the union of all, let us pray to the Lord.
For this holy house and for those who enter it with faith, reverence, and the fear of God, let us pray to the Lord.
@@hierarch-commemoration.greatLitany
For this country, its President [or: the civil authorities], for all civil authorities, and for the armed forces, let us pray to the Lord.
For this city [or: village, or: holy monastery], every city and countryside, and the faithful who dwell therein, let us pray to the Lord.
For seasonable weather, an abundance of the fruits of the earth, and for peaceful times, let us pray to the Lord.
For travelers by sea, by land, and by air; for the sick and the suffering; for captives and for their salvation, let us pray to the Lord.
For our deliverance from all tribulation, wrath, danger, and necessity, let us pray to the Lord.
Help us, save us, have mercy on us, and keep us, O God, by Thy grace.
great-litany.commemoration: Commemorating our most holy, most pure, most blessed and glorious Lady Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary, with all the saints, let us commend ourselves and each other and all our life unto Christ our God.
great-litany.exclamation: For unto Thee are due all glory, honor, and worship: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

typical-antiphon-1._note: Psalm 102 — typical First Antiphon, sung when no feast antiphon is appointed. OCA Typika translation. Line breaks within a verse correspond to '*' breath/musical breaks in the source.
typical-antiphon-1.refrain: Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us.
verses:
Bless the Lord, O my soul. Blessed art thou, O Lord.
Bless the Lord, O my soul; and all that is within me, bless his holy name.
Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits,

who forgives all your iniquities, who heals all your diseases,
who redeems your life from the pit, who crowns you with steadfast love and mercy,
who satisfies you with good as long as you live, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle's.

The Lord works vindication and justice for the oppressed.
He made known his ways to Moses, his acts to the people of Israel.

The Lord is compassionate and merciful, long-suffering and of great goodness.
He will not always chide, nor will he keep his anger forever.
The Lord has established his throne in the heavens, and his kingdom rules over all.

Bless the Lord, O you his angels, you mighty ones who do his word,
hearkening to the voice of his word.
Bless the Lord, all his hosts, his ministers that do his will.
Bless the Lord, all his works, in all places of his dominion.

Bless the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me,
bless his holy name.
Blessed art thou, O Lord!
typical-antiphon-1.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
typical-antiphon-1.gloryRefrain: Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us.

little-litany.opening: Again and again in peace, let us pray to the Lord.
little-litany.petition: Help us, save us, have mercy on us, and keep us, O God, by Thy grace.
little-litany.commemoration: Commemorating our most holy, most pure, most blessed and glorious Lady Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary, with all the saints, let us commend ourselves and each other and all our life unto Christ our God.
little-litany.exclamation1: For Thine is the might, and Thine is the Kingdom, and the power, and the glory: of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.
little-litany.exclamation2: For Thou art a holy God, and unto Thee do we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

typical-antiphon-2._note: Psalm 145 — typical Second Antiphon, sung when no feast antiphon is appointed. OCA Typika translation. Line breaks within a verse correspond to '*' breath/musical breaks in the source.
typical-antiphon-2.refrain: Save us, O Son of God, who art risen from the dead, who sing to Thee: Alleluia.
typical-antiphon-2.refrainWeekday: Save us, O Son of God, who art wondrous in Thy saints, who sing to Thee: Alleluia.
verses:
Praise the Lord, O my soul.
I will praise the Lord as long as I live; I will sing praises to my God while I have being.

Put not your trust in princes, in sons of men, in whom there is no salvation.
When his breath departs, he returns to his earth; on that very day his plans perish.

Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the Lord his God,
who made heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them;

The Lord sets the prisoners free; the Lord opens the eyes of the blind.
The Lord lifts up those who are bowed down; the Lord loves the righteous.

The Lord watches over the sojourners, he upholds the widow and the fatherless;
but the way of the wicked he will bring to ruin.
The Lord will reign forever,
thy God, O Zion, to all generations.
typical-antiphon-2.glory: Now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

only-begotten-son: Only-begotten Son and immortal Word of God, Who for our salvation didst will to be incarnate of the holy Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary, Who without change didst become man and wast crucified, O Christ our God, trampling down death by death, Who art one of the Holy Trinity, glorified with the Father and the Holy Spirit: save us.

kontakion-theotokion._note: Standard Sunday Theotokion-Kontakion, sung at 'Now and ever...' to close the Kontakia at the Liturgy after the saint kontakion. Romanos the Melodist's 'Protection of Christians' (Greek: 'Προστασία τῶν Χριστιανῶν'). OCA translation.
kontakion-theotokion.text: Protection of Christians that cannot be put to shame, mediation unto the Creator immovable: O despise not the suppliant voices of those who have sinned; but be thou quick, O good one, to come unto our aid, who in faith cry unto thee: Hasten to intercession, and speed thou to make supplication, O Theotokos, who dost ever protect those who honor thee.

beatitudes._note: Matthew 5:3–12. Troparia are interspersed between verses starting at the slot indicated by the calendar. Direction: top-down (verse 1 is first, last verse is 'Theotokion'). Translation: HTM (Holy Transfiguration Monastery, Boston) style — literal Greek 'Kingdom of the Heavens', 'sated', archaic 'they that...'.
verses: In Thy Kingdom, remember us, O Lord, when Thou comest in Thy Kingdom.
Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of the Heavens.
Blessed are they that mourn, for they shall be comforted.
Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.
Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be sated.
Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the sons of God.
Blessed are they that are persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of the Heavens.
Blessed are ye when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for My sake.
Rejoice, and be exceeding glad, for great is your reward in the heavens.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.
Now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

small-entrance.silentPrayer: O Master and Lord our God, Who hast appointed in the heavens orders and armies of angels and archangels for the service of Thy glory: grant that with our entrance there may be an entrance of holy angels serving with us and glorifying Thy goodness. For to Thee are due all glory, honor, and worship: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

augmented-litany._note: Also called the Litany of Fervent Supplication. Responses alternate between Lord, have mercy (single) and Lord, have mercy (×3). Per OCA Service Book / Liturgikon, no Theotokos commemoration is appended in this litany.
augmented-litany.opening: Let us say with all our soul and with all our mind, let us say:
petitions: O Lord Almighty, the God of our fathers, we pray Thee, hearken and have mercy.
Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great goodness, we pray Thee, hearken and have mercy.
augmented-litany.tripleResponse: Lord, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.
triplePetitions: Again we pray for this country, its President [or: the civil authorities], and for the armed forces.
Again we pray for the mercy, life, peace, health, salvation, and visitation of the servants of God, all pious and Orthodox Christians dwelling in this city and in all the world.

Again we pray for the blessed and ever-memorable holy Orthodox Patriarchs; and for the founders of this holy temple [or: monastery]; and for all our fathers and brethren who have before us fallen asleep in the hope of resurrection and life eternal.

Again we pray for those who bring offerings and do good works in this holy and all-venerable temple; for those who labor and those who sing; and for all the people here present, who await from Thee great and abundant mercy.
augmented-litany.exclamation: For Thou art a merciful God and lovest mankind, and unto Thee do we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

litany-departed._note: Optional litany for the departed, inserted between Augmented Litany and Litany for the Catechumens. Used on Soul Saturdays and other commemorations of the departed.
litany-departed.opening: Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy, we pray Thee, hearken and have mercy.
litany-departed.tripleResponse: Lord, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.
petitions: Again we pray for the repose of the souls of the departed servants of God (N.), and that they may be forgiven every transgression, both voluntary and involuntary.
That the Lord God will commit their souls to where the righteous repose.
litany-departed.askPetition: The mercy of God, the kingdom of heaven, and the remission of their sins, let us ask of Christ the Immortal King and our God.
litany-departed.deaconCall: Let us pray to the Lord.
litany-departed.secretPrayer: O God of spirits and of all flesh, Who hast trampled down death by death, and overthrown the devil, and given life to Thy world: Do Thou Thyself, O Lord, give rest to the souls of Thy departed servants (N.), in a place of light, a place of green pasture, a place of repose, whence all sickness, sorrow and sighing are fled away. Pardon every sin committed by them in word, deed, or thought, in that Thou art a good God, and the Lover of mankind; for there is no man that liveth and sinneth not, for Thou art alone without sin, Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and Thy word is truth.
litany-departed.exclamation: For Thou art the resurrection, and the life, and the repose of Thy departed servants (N.), O Christ our God, and unto Thee do we send up glory, together with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thy most holy and good and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages.

litany-catechumens.opening: Pray to the Lord, ye catechumens.
petitions: Let us, the faithful, pray for the catechumens.
That the Lord will have mercy on them.
That He will teach them the word of truth.
That He will reveal to them the Gospel of righteousness.
That He will unite them to His holy, catholic, and apostolic Church.
litany-catechumens.petition2: Save them, have mercy on them, help them, and keep them, O God, by Thy grace.
litany-catechumens.bowHeads: Bow your heads before the Lord, ye catechumens.
litany-catechumens.exclamation: That they also, with us, may glorify Thy most honorable and majestic name: of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.
litany-catechumens.dismissal: As many as are catechumens, depart! Depart, catechumens! As many as are catechumens, depart! Let none of the catechumens remain!

litany-faithful-1._note: First Litany of the Faithful per OCA Liturgikon. No Theotokos commemoration. Deacon's 'Wisdom!' precedes the priest's exclamation.
litany-faithful-1.opening: We, the faithful, again and again in peace, let us pray to the Lord.
litany-faithful-1.petition: Help us, save us, have mercy on us, and keep us, O God, by Thy grace.
litany-faithful-1.exclamation: For all glory, honor, and worship are due unto Thee: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

litany-faithful-2._note: Second Litany of the Faithful per OCA Liturgikon (long form): the deacon prefaces with 'Wisdom!' and recites the great-litany-style petitions before 'Help us, save us...' Then a second 'Wisdom!' introduces the priest's exclamation. No Theotokos commemoration.
litany-faithful-2.opening: Again and again in peace, let us pray to the Lord.
petitions: For the peace from above, and for the salvation of our souls, let us pray to the Lord.
For the peace of the whole world, the good estate of the holy churches of God, and the union of all, let us pray to the Lord.
For this holy temple, and for those who enter with faith, reverence, and the fear of God, let us pray to the Lord.
For our deliverance from all tribulation, wrath, danger, and necessity, let us pray to the Lord.
litany-faithful-2.petition: Help us, save us, have mercy on us, and keep us, O God, by Thy grace.
litany-faithful-2.exclamation: That guarded always by Thy might, we may ascribe glory unto Thee: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

cherubic-hymn._setting_label: Plain prose text (no musical repetitions or held-note markers)
cherubic-hymn._source: OCA / Antiochian Liturgikon — 'We, who mystically represent the Cherubim' translation
cherubic-hymn.part1: We, who mystically represent the Cherubim, and who sing to the Life-creating Trinity the thrice-holy hymn, let us now lay aside all earthly cares.
cherubic-hymn.part2: That we may receive the King of all, Who cometh invisibly upborne by the angelic hosts.

cherubic-hymn-tchaikovsky._setting_label: Tchaikovsky setting; English paraphrase by D G M
cherubic-hymn-tchaikovsky.part1:
All we who represent, represent the Cherubim, the Cherubim here on earth in mystic form
sing unto the life-giving Trinity, sing unto the life-giving Trinity,
the thrice holy hymn, the thrice holy hymn,
the thrice holy hymn to the Trinity, the thrice holy hymn to the Trinity.
Let us now lay aside, lay aside all care,
let us lay aside, lay aside all earthly care,
lay, lay aside, aside all earthly care.
cherubic-hymn-tchaikovsky.part2:
That we may receive the King of all, we may receive the King,
the King of all in glory,
Who comes invisible borne in triumph by the ranks of angels,
by the ranks of angels.

cherubic-hymn-lvovsky._setting_label: L'vovsky / Greek Chant setting; em-dash extensions ≈ held beats in the soprano line
cherubic-hymn-lvovsky.part1:
Let——— us who mys-tic'-ly, mys-tic'-ly re——— pre-sent the Che——ru-bim, the Che——ru-bim,
and who sing the thrice—— ho——————— ly hymn, and who sing the thrice—— ho——————— ly hymn,
to the life-cre-a-ting, life-cre-a-ting Trin———i-ty,
now——— lay a-side, lay a-side all cares,— now——— lay a-side all earth-ly cares,— all earth-ly cares.———
cherubic-hymn-lvovsky.part2:
That we may re-ceive, re-ceive the King of all,
Who comes in-vi-si-bly, in-vi-si-bly up-borne
by the an-gel-ic hosts, by the an-gel-ic hosts.

cherubic-great-thursday:
Of Thy mystical Supper, O Son of God, accept me today as a communicant; for I will not speak of Thy mystery to Thine enemies; neither will I give Thee a kiss as did Judas; but like the thief will I confess Thee: Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom.

Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom. Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom.
cherubic-great-saturday: Let all mortal flesh keep silent, and in fear and trembling stand, pondering nothing earthly-minded. For the King of kings, the Lord of lords, comes to be slain, to give Himself as food to the faithful. Before Him go the ranks of angels, all the Principalities and Powers, the many-eyed Cherubim and the six-winged Seraphim, covering their faces, singing the hymn: Alleluia! Alleluia! Alleluia!

readings._note: Short overlay-translatable strings used by the readings flow (Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel). Templated strings use `(book)` as a substitution token, matching the `(name)` convention used by general-menaion fallbacks.
readings.wisdomAriseGospel: Wisdom! Arise! Let us hear the Holy Gospel.
readings.gloryToTheeOLord: Glory to Thee, O Lord, glory to Thee.
readings.gospelReadingFromTemplate: The reading of the Holy Gospel according to (book).

great-entrance._note: The deacon and priest carry the Holy Gifts through the nave. The commemorations are variable.
great-entrance.commonCommemoration: All of you Orthodox Christians, may the Lord God remember in His Kingdom, always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

litany-supplication._note: Sung after the Great Entrance and the closing of the Holy Doors.
litany-supplication.opening: Let us complete our prayer unto the Lord.
petitions: For the precious Gifts here offered, let us pray to the Lord.
For this holy house and for those who enter it with faith, reverence, and the fear of God, let us pray to the Lord.
For our deliverance from all tribulation, wrath, danger, and necessity, let us pray to the Lord.
Help us, save us, have mercy on us, and keep us, O God, by Thy grace.
petitions2: That the whole day may be perfect, holy, peaceful, and sinless, let us ask of the Lord.
An angel of peace, a faithful guide, a guardian of our souls and bodies, let us ask of the Lord.
Pardon and remission of our sins and transgressions, let us ask of the Lord.
All things that are good and profitable for our souls, and peace for the world, let us ask of the Lord.
That we may complete the remaining time of our life in peace and repentance, let us ask of the Lord.
A Christian ending to our life: painless, blameless, and peaceful; and a good defense before the dread judgment seat of Christ, let us ask.
litany-supplication.commemoration: Commemorating our most holy, most pure, most blessed and glorious Lady Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary, with all the saints, let us commend ourselves and each other and all our life unto Christ our God.
litany-supplication.exclamation: Through the mercies of Thine Only-begotten Son, with Whom Thou art blessed, together with Thine all-holy, good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

kiss-of-peace._note: Said immediately before the Creed. Deacon's call, people's response, then deacon's 'The doors!' before the Creed begins.
kiss-of-peace.deaconCall: Let us love one another, that with one mind we may confess:
kiss-of-peace.response: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit: the Trinity, one in essence and undivided.
kiss-of-peace.doors: The doors! The doors! In wisdom let us attend!

creed:
I believe in one God, the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth and of all things visible and invisible.

And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the Only-begotten, begotten of the Father before all ages; Light of Light, true God of true God; begotten, not made; of one essence with the Father; by whom all things were made; who for us men and for our salvation came down from heaven, and was incarnate of the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary, and became man; and he was crucified for us under Pontius Pilate, and suffered, and was buried; and the third day he rose again, according to the Scriptures, and ascended into heaven, and sits at the right hand of the Father; and he shall come again with glory to judge the living and the dead; whose kingdom shall have no end.

And in the Holy Spirit, the Lord, the Giver of life, who proceeds from the Father; who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified; who spoke by the prophets.

In One, Holy, Catholic, and Apostolic Church. I acknowledge one baptism for the remission of sins. I look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the age to come. Amen.

anaphora-opening._note: Deacon's call and people's response immediately before the Sursum Corda. Same for Chrysostom and Basil.
anaphora-opening.deaconCall: Let us stand aright; let us stand in fear; let us attend, that we may offer the Holy Oblation in peace.
anaphora-opening.response: A mercy of peace, a sacrifice of praise.

anaphora-chrysostom._note: The Anaphora of St. John Chrysostom. Silent prayers are indicated in rubrics. Only the audible/sung portions are stored here.

sursum-corda.speaker: priest
sursum-corda.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God the Father, and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with you all.

sursum-corda.speaker: priest
sursum-corda.text: Let us lift up our hearts.

sursum-corda.speaker: people
sursum-corda.text: We lift them up unto the Lord.

sursum-corda.speaker: priest
sursum-corda.text: Let us give thanks unto the Lord.

sursum-corda.speaker: people
sursum-corda.text: It is meet and right to worship Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, the Trinity, one in essence and undivided.

anaphora-chrysostom.preface: It is meet and right to hymn Thee, to bless Thee, to praise Thee, to give thanks unto Thee, and to worship Thee in every place of Thy dominion: for Thou art God ineffable, inconceivable, invisible, incomprehensible, ever-existing and eternally the same, Thou and Thine Only-begotten Son and Thy Holy Spirit. Thou it was Who didst bring us from non-existence into being, and when we had fallen away didst raise us up again, and didst not cease to do all things until Thou hadst brought us up to heaven and hadst endowed us with Thy Kingdom which is to come. For all these things we give thanks unto Thee, and to Thine Only-begotten Son, and to Thy Holy Spirit; for all things of which we know and of which we know not, whether manifest or unseen; and we thank Thee for this Liturgy which Thou hast been pleased to accept at our hands, though there stand by Thee thousands of archangels and ten thousands of angels, the cherubim and the seraphim, six-winged, many-eyed, soaring aloft upon their pinions,
anaphora-chrysostom.sanctus-introduction: singing the triumphal hymn, shouting, crying aloud, and saying:
anaphora-chrysostom.sanctus: Holy, holy, holy, Lord of Sabaoth! Heaven and earth are full of Thy glory! Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!
anaphora-chrysostom.post-sanctus: With these blessed hosts, O Master, Lover of mankind, we also cry aloud and say: Holy art Thou and most holy, Thou, and Thine only-begotten Son, and Thy Holy Spirit: holy art Thou and most holy, and majestic is Thy glory, O Thou Who so loved Thy world that Thou gavest Thine Only-begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life; Who when He had come and fulfilled all the dispensation for us, on the night in which He was betrayed, or rather gave Himself up for the life of the world, took bread in His holy and most pure and unblemished hands, and when He had given thanks, and had blessed it, and hallowed it, and broken it, He gave it to His holy disciples and apostles, saying:
anaphora-chrysostom.institution-body: Take, eat, this is My Body, which is broken for you, for the forgiveness of sins.
anaphora-chrysostom.institution-cup: Drink of it, all of you; this is My Blood of the New Testament, which is shed for you and for many, for the forgiveness of sins.
anaphora-chrysostom.anamnesis-prayer: Remembering, therefore, this saving commandment, and all those things which came to pass for us: the Cross, the Grave, the Resurrection on the third day, the Ascension into Heaven, the Sitting on the right hand, and the Second and Glorious Coming again,
anaphora-chrysostom.anamnesis: Thine own of Thine own, we offer unto Thee, on behalf of all and for all.
anaphora-chrysostom.anamnesis-response: We hymn Thee, we bless Thee, we give thanks to Thee, O Lord, and we pray unto Thee, O our God.

epiclesis._note: The Epiclesis — invocation of the Holy Spirit upon the gifts. Priest prays the opening invocation (in many parishes silently); a short dialogue with the deacon follows over the bread and the cup, with the choir's triple Amen at the consecration.
epiclesis.invocation: Once again we offer unto Thee this rational and bloodless worship, and we beseech Thee, and we pray Thee, and we entreat Thee: send down Thy Holy Spirit upon us and upon these gifts here offered.

exchanges.speaker: priest
exchanges.text: And make this bread the precious Body of Thy Christ.

exchanges.speaker: priest
exchanges.text: And that which is in this cup, the precious Blood of Thy Christ.

exchanges.speaker: priest
exchanges.text: Changing them by Thy Holy Spirit.

epiclesis.fruits: So that they may be to those who partake, for the purification of soul, for the remission of sins, for the communion of Thy Holy Spirit, for the fulfillment of the Kingdom of Heaven, for boldness toward Thee, and not for judgment or condemnation.

anaphora-chrysostom.commemoration-saints: Again we offer unto Thee this rational worship for those who have departed in the faith: forefathers, fathers, patriarchs, prophets, apostles, preachers, evangelists, martyrs, confessors, ascetics, and for every righteous spirit made perfect in faith.
anaphora-chrysostom.megalynarion-cue: Especially for our most holy, most pure, most blessed and glorious Lady Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary.
anaphora-chrysostom.commemoration-hierarchs: Among the first remember, O Lord, our Metropolitan [N.], our Archbishop [N.], and our Bishop [N.], whom do Thou grant unto Thy holy churches in peace, safety, honor, and health, for many years, rightly defining the word of Thy truth.
anaphora-chrysostom.intercessions-exclamation: And grant that with one mouth and one heart we may glorify and hymn Thine all-honorable and majestic Name: of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.
anaphora-chrysostom.final-blessing: And the mercies of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ be with you all.

anaphora-basil._note: The Anaphora of St. Basil the Great. Shares the same sursum corda as Chrysostom. The preface and intercessions are significantly expanded.

sursum-corda.speaker: priest
sursum-corda.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God the Father, and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with you all.

sursum-corda.speaker: priest
sursum-corda.text: Let us lift up our hearts.

sursum-corda.speaker: people
sursum-corda.text: We lift them up unto the Lord.

sursum-corda.speaker: priest
sursum-corda.text: Let us give thanks unto the Lord.

sursum-corda.speaker: people
sursum-corda.text: It is meet and right to worship Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, the Trinity, one in essence and undivided.

anaphora-basil.preface-incipit: O Thou Who art, Master, Lord, God, Father Almighty, and adorable; it is truly meet and right and befitting the magnificence of Thy holiness to praise Thee, to hymn Thee, to bless Thee, to worship Thee, to give thanks to Thee, to glorify Thee Who alone art truly God…
anaphora-basil.sanctus-introduction: …and with thousands of Archangels and ten thousands of Angels, with the Cherubim and Seraphim, Who are six-winged and many-eyed, soaring aloft, borne on their wings, singing the triumphal hymn, shouting, crying aloud, and saying:
anaphora-basil.sanctus: Holy, holy, holy, Lord of Sabaoth! Heaven and earth are full of Thy glory! Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!
anaphora-basil.institution-body: Take, eat, this is My Body, which is broken for you, for the forgiveness of sins.
anaphora-basil.institution-cup: Drink of it, all of you; this is My Blood of the New Testament, which is shed for you and for many, for the forgiveness of sins.
anaphora-basil.anamnesis-prayer: Therefore, O Master, we also, remembering His saving Passion and life-giving Cross, His three-day Burial and Resurrection from the dead, His Ascension into heaven, and Sitting at the right hand of Thee, the God and Father, and His glorious and dread Second Coming;
anaphora-basil.anamnesis: Thine own of Thine own, we offer unto Thee, on behalf of all and for all.
anaphora-basil.anamnesis-response: We hymn Thee, we bless Thee, we give thanks to Thee, O Lord, and we pray unto Thee, O our God.
anaphora-basil.megalynarion-cue: Especially for our most holy, most pure, most blessed and glorious Lady Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary.
anaphora-basil.intercessions-exclamation: And grant that with one mouth and one heart we may glorify and hymn Thine all-honorable and majestic Name: of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.
anaphora-basil.final-blessing: And the mercies of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ be with you all.

it-is-truly-meet: It is truly meet to bless thee, O Theotokos, ever-blessed and most pure and the Mother of our God. More honorable than the Cherubim, and more glorious beyond compare than the Seraphim; without defilement thou gavest birth to God the Word: true Theotokos, we magnify thee.
megalynarion-basil: All of creation rejoices in thee, O Full of Grace: the assembly of angels and the race of men. O sanctified temple and spiritual paradise, the glory of virgins, from whom God was incarnate and became a Child: our God before the ages. He made thy body into a throne, and thy womb He made more spacious than the heavens. All of creation rejoices in thee, O Full of Grace. Glory to thee!
megalynarion-paschal:
The Angel cried to the Lady, full of grace:
"Rejoice, O pure Virgin! Again, I say: Rejoice,
thy Son is risen from His three days in the tomb!
With Himself He has raised all the dead."
Rejoice, O ye people!

Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem!
The glory of the Lord has shone on thee.
Exult now, and be glad, O Zion!
Be radiant, O pure Theotokos,
in the Resurrection of thy Son!

litany-lords-prayer.opening: Having remembered all the saints, again and again in peace, let us pray to the Lord.
petitions: For the precious Gifts offered and sanctified, let us pray to the Lord.

That our God, Who loveth mankind, receiving them upon His holy, heavenly, and ideal altar as a sweet spiritual fragrance, will send down upon us in return His divine grace and the gift of the Holy Spirit, let us pray to the Lord.
For our deliverance from all affliction, wrath, danger, and necessity, let us pray to the Lord.
Help us, save us, have mercy on us, and keep us, O God, by Thy grace.
That the whole day may be perfect, holy, peaceful, and sinless, let us ask of the Lord.
An angel of peace, a faithful guide, a guardian of our souls and bodies, let us ask of the Lord.
Pardon and remission of our sins and transgressions, let us ask of the Lord.
All things that are good and profitable for our souls, and peace for the world, let us ask of the Lord.
That we may complete the remaining time of our life in peace and repentance, let us ask of the Lord.
A Christian ending to our life: painless, blameless, and peaceful; and a good defense before the dread judgment seat of Christ, let us ask.
litany-lords-prayer.commemoration: Having asked for the unity of the faith and the communion of the Holy Spirit, let us commend ourselves and each other and all our life unto Christ our God.
litany-lords-prayer.exclamation-chrysostom: And make us worthy, O Master, that with boldness and without condemnation, we may dare to call on Thee, the heavenly God, as Father, and to say:
litany-lords-prayer.exclamation-basil: And make us worthy, O Master, that with boldness and without condemnation we may dare to call on Thee, the heavenly God, as Father, and to say:

lords-prayer.text: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy Name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread; and forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.
lords-prayer.doxology: For Thine is the Kingdom, and the power, and the glory, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

pre-communion._note: The pre-communion prayer said/sung by all before receiving Holy Communion. Two OCA-approved translations are provided.

bowHeads.deacon: Bow your heads unto the Lord.

pre-communion.bow-prayer-chrysostom: We give thanks unto Thee, O King invisible, Who by Thy measureless power didst make all things, and in the greatness of Thy mercy didst bring all things from non-existence into being. Do Thou Thyself, O Master, look down from heaven upon those who have bowed their heads before Thee; for they have bowed not before flesh and blood, but before Thee, the awesome God. Do Thou, O Master, distribute these Gifts here offered unto all of us for good, according to the individual need of each; sail with those who sail, travel with those who travel by land and by air; heal the sick, O Thou Who art the Physician of our souls and bodies.
pre-communion.bow-prayer-basil: O Master, Lord, Father of compassions and God of every consolation: Bless, sanctify, guard, strengthen, and confirm those who have bowed their heads before Thee. Withdraw them from every evil deed; apply them to every good work and make them worthy to partake without condemnation of these, Thy most pure and life-creating Mysteries, for remission of sins and for the communion of the Holy Spirit.

elevation.priest: The holy Things are for the holy!
elevation.people: One is holy, one is Lord, Jesus Christ, to the glory of God the Father. Amen.

pre-communion.drawNear: In the fear of God and with faith, draw near!
pre-communion.blessedIsHe: Blessed is He that comes in the Name of the Lord; God is the Lord and has revealed Himself unto us!
pre-communion.prayer-chrysostom:
I believe, O Lord, and I confess that Thou art truly the Christ, the Son of the Living God, Who camest into the world to save sinners, of whom I am first. I believe also that this is truly Thine own pure Body, and that this is truly Thine own precious Blood. Therefore I pray Thee: have mercy upon me and forgive my transgressions both voluntary and involuntary, of word and of deed, of knowledge and of ignorance. And make me worthy to partake without condemnation of Thy most pure Mysteries, for the remission of my sins, and unto life everlasting. Amen.

Of Thy Mystical Supper, O Son of God, accept me today as a communicant; for I will not speak of Thy Mystery to Thine enemies, neither like Judas will I give Thee a kiss; but like the thief will I confess Thee: Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom.

May the communion of Thy Holy Mysteries be neither to my judgment, nor to my condemnation, O Lord, but to the healing of soul and body. Amen.
pre-communion.prayer-basil: O God, the God of salvation, do Thou teach us to thank Thee worthily for the benefits which Thou hast performed for us and still performest with us. Having accepted these Gifts, O our God, do Thou purify us from every defilement of flesh and spirit, and teach us how to perfect our sanctification in Thy fear, so that receiving a portion of Thy Holy Things with a pure conscience we may be united with the Holy Body and Blood of Thy Christ. Having received them worthily, may we have Christ dwelling in our hearts, and may we become the temple of Thy Holy Spirit. Yea, O our God, let none of us be guilty of these Thine awesome and heavenly Mysteries, nor be infirm in soul and body by partaking of them unworthily. But, enable us, even to our last breath, to receive a portion of Thy Holy Things worthily, as a support on the road to eternal life and an acceptable defense at the dread judgment seat of Thy Christ.

communion-of-faithful._note: Hymns sung while the faithful approach the chalice, after the Koinonikon. 'Body of Christ' is the standard refrain in most OCA parishes; the paschal form replaces it from Pascha through Leavetaking. 'Receive me today' is offered as an opt-in alternate for parishes that sing the festal Mystical Supper hymn here.
communion-of-faithful.rubric: During the Communion of the Faithful:
communion-of-faithful.body-of-christ: Body of Christ, receive; taste of the fountain of immortality.
communion-of-faithful.body-of-christ-paschal: Receive ye the Body of Christ; taste ye of the fountain of immortality.
communion-of-faithful.receive-me-today: Of Thy Mystical Supper, O Son of God, receive me today as a communicant; for I will not speak of Thy Mystery to Thine enemies, neither like Judas will I give Thee a kiss; but like the thief will I confess Thee: Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom.
communion-of-faithful.troparia-rubric: The Troparia and Kontakia of the day may also be repeated, along with other hymns appropriate to the feast.

post-communion-blessing.priest: Save, O God, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance.
post-communion-blessing.people: We have seen the true Light! We have received the heavenly Spirit! We have found the true Faith! Worshiping the undivided Trinity, Who hath saved us.
post-communion-blessing._note: The priest says the exclamation while carrying the Holy Gifts to the Table of Oblation.

we-have-seen: We have seen the true Light. We have received the heavenly Spirit. We have found the true Faith, worshiping the undivided Trinity, Who has saved us.
christ-is-risen: Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life. Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life. Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life.
always-now-and-ever: Always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.
let-our-mouths: Let our mouths be filled with Thy praise, O Lord, that we may sing of Thy glory; for Thou hast made us worthy to partake of Thy holy, divine, immortal, and life-creating Mysteries. Keep us in Thy holiness, that all the day we may meditate upon Thy righteousness. Alleluia! Alleluia! Alleluia!

litany-thanksgiving.deacon: Let us attend. Having partaken of the divine, holy, most-pure, immortal, heavenly, and life-creating, awesome Mysteries of Christ, let us worthily give thanks unto the Lord.
litany-thanksgiving.petition: Help us, save us, have mercy on us, and keep us, O God, by Thy grace.
petitions: That the whole day may be perfect, holy, peaceful, and sinless, let us ask of the Lord.
An angel of peace, a faithful guide, a guardian of our souls and bodies, let us ask of the Lord.
Pardon and remission of our sins and transgressions, let us ask of the Lord.
All things that are good and profitable for our souls, and peace for the world, let us ask of the Lord.
That we may complete the remaining time of our life in peace and repentance, let us ask of the Lord.
A Christian ending to our life: painless, blameless, and peaceful; and a good defense before the dread judgment seat of Christ, let us ask.
litany-thanksgiving.commemoration: Having asked for the unity of the faith and the communion of the Holy Spirit, let us commend ourselves and each other and all our life unto Christ our God.
litany-thanksgiving.exclamation: For Thou art our sanctification, and unto Thee do we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.
litany-thanksgiving.prayer-chrysostom: We thank Thee, O Master Who lovest mankind, Benefactor of our souls, that Thou hast made us worthy this day of Thy heavenly and immortal Mysteries. Make straight our path; strengthen us all in Thy fear; guard our life; make firm our steps; through the prayers and intercessions of the glorious Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary, and of all Thy saints.
litany-thanksgiving.prayer-basil: We thank Thee, O Lord our God, for the participation in Thy holy, most-pure, immortal and heavenly Mysteries, which Thou hast granted us for the good and sanctification and healing of our souls and bodies. Do Thou, O Master of all, grant that the communion of the Holy Body and Blood of Thy Christ may be to us for a faith unashamed, a love unfeigned, an increase of wisdom, the healing of soul and body, the repelling of every adversary, the observance of Thy commandments, and an acceptable defense at the dread judgment seat of Thy Christ.

prayer-ambon-chrysostom: O Lord, Who blessest those who bless Thee, and sanctifiest those who put their trust in Thee: save Thy people and bless Thine inheritance; preserve the fullness of Thy Church; sanctify those who love the beauty of Thy house; glorify them in return by Thy divine power, and forsake us not who set our hope on Thee. Give peace to Thy world, to Thy churches, to the clergy, to those who govern us, to the armed forces, and to all Thy people. For every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from Thee, the Father of lights. And to Thee do we send up glory, thanksgiving, and worship: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.
prayer-ambon-basil: O Lord, Who blessest those who bless Thee, and sanctifiest those who put their trust in Thee: save Thy people and bless Thine inheritance; preserve the fullness of Thy Church; sanctify those who love the beauty of Thy house. Do Thou glorify them in return by Thy divine power, and forsake us not who set our hope in Thee. Give peace to Thy world, to Thy churches, to the priests, to those in authority, to the armed forces, and to all Thy people. For every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from Thee, the Father of lights; and unto Thee do we ascribe glory, thanksgiving, and worship: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

blessed-be-the-name.text: Blessed be the name of the Lord, henceforth and forevermore.
blessed-be-the-name.finalBlessing: The blessing of the Lord be upon you, through His grace and love for mankind, always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

psalm-33._note: Read by the reader while the priest reads the Prayer of Thanksgiving behind the altar. Psalm 33 (LXX)/Psalm 34 (Hebrew), abbreviated to OCA parish practice: verses 1–3, verse 8 ('O taste and see...'), and verses 9–10. Omits verses 4–7 only.
psalm-33.text:
I will bless the Lord at all times; His praise shall continually be in my mouth. In the Lord shall my soul make her boast; the humble shall hear thereof, and be glad. O magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt His name together.

O taste and see that the Lord is good; blessed is the man that hopeth in Him.

O fear the Lord, ye His saints; for there is no want to them that fear Him. The rich have become poor, and hunger; but they that seek the Lord shall not want any good thing.
psalm-33.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

troparion-chrysostom.troparion: Grace shining forth from thy lips like a beacon hath illumined the universe, and disclosed to the world the treasures of non-covetousness, and shown us the heights of humility; but whilst thine own words teach us, O Father John Chrysostom, intercede with the Word, Christ our God, to save our souls.

troparion-basil.troparion: Thy proclamation has gone out into all the earth, which has received thy word. Thereby thou hast divinely taught the Faith; thou hast made manifest the nature of created things; thou hast made the moral life of men a royal priesthood. O Basil, our righteous father, intercede with Christ God that our souls may be saved.

dismissal-theotokion: O protection of Christians that cannot be put to shame, O mediation unto the Creator most constant: despise not the suppliant voices of those who have sinned; but be thou quick, O good one, to come unto our aid, who in faith cry unto thee: Hasten to intercession, and speed thou to make supplication, thou who dost ever protect, O Theotokos, them that honor thee.

trisagion.text: Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us.
trisagion.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
trisagion.final: Holy Immortal, have mercy on us.

trisagion-cross.text: Before Thy Cross, we bow down in worship, O Master, and Thy holy Resurrection we glorify.
trisagion-cross.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
trisagion-cross.final: And Thy holy Resurrection we glorify.

trisagion-baptismal.text: As many as have been baptized into Christ, have put on Christ. Alleluia.
trisagion-baptismal.glory: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
